summary: We are testing whether doubling the MaxRects heuristic palette from 4 to 8 options (adding perimeter-sum fit, top-right, left-bottom x-primary, aspect-ratio fit) combined with per-item rotation mode as a new SA search dimension can push the score beyond the current best of 95.21. A control arm isolates whether the expanded heuristic set or the SA tuning changes (faster cooling at 0.995, 3 restarts, reheat every 500 steps) are the primary driver of improvement.
key_points: Main arm (h-main): 8 MaxRects heuristics × 3 rotation modes per item, SA with cooling=0.995, 3 restarts, reheat every 500 iters. Predicted score ~96.4 (up from 95.21).

Control arm (h-control-negative): Same SA tuning but only the original 4 heuristics, keeping rotation mode. If this matches h-main, the new heuristics are redundant and SA tuning alone explains gains; if it stays near 95.21, expanded heuristics are the key lever.
Confirmation criterion: h-main scores ≥96.0 AND h-main exceeds h-control by ≥0.5 points, demonstrating that the expanded heuristic space is a necessary contributor beyond SA tuning alone.

Refutation signals: (1) h-main ≤ 95.5 means neither change helps meaningfully; (2) h-control matches h-main means new heuristics are redundant; (3) h-main improves but h-control also improves similarly means SA tuning is the real driver.

Risk: 1-second time limit is tight for 3 SA restarts over a 24^M search space; if timeouts occur on large tests, scores will drop to 0 on those cases. The diagnostic is to check per-test scores for zeros.
